title: E0094: Denial of Service via Regular Expression
plain_english: User-supplied regular expressions, or regex patterns applied to user input, can cause catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS), consuming CPU and making the application unavailable.
why_matters: ReDoS can cause CPU spikes and denial of service. A single malicious request may keep a worker busy for seconds or minutes, exhausting application capacity.
what_it_checks: Nested quantifiers in regex patterns, such as `(a+)+`, `(a*)*`, `(a|b)+`
User-supplied regex patterns passed to `preg_match()`, `preg_replace()`, or `preg_split()`
`preg_match()` on very long user input without timeout
